user.t:
Council position (read-only, concise) on: take all 11 pre-product B2B SaaS marketing sites LIVE via GitHub Pages now? Facts: honest pre-product/design-partner static sites under marketing/site/ (no fabricated metrics, DRAFT legal, placeholder contact); repos private; option = separate PUBLIC site-only repo per business + Pages.
From the growth/go-to-market lens: does a live site actually help design-partner outreach for a pre-product B2B tool, or is a landing page without a product premature? What's the minimum that makes a live site useful (real contact/CTA, a way to capture interest without a fake signup), and would you launch all 11 at once or pilot 1-2? Concise, honest (no growth-hacking that implies the product is live). Return a short position + recommendation.

handback.t:
## Herald Position: Take the 11 pre-product sites live on GitHub Pages?

**Core recommendation:** Pilot 1-2 sites now; hold the other 9 until the pilots show the live site actually helps outreach. A live site is useful for design-partner outreach only as a credibility checkpoint. It is not a growth channel, and it should be treated that way.

**Does a live site help, or is it premature?**
- In B2B design-partner outreach the site is a verification step, not an acquisition channel. A prospect gets a cold email or DM, then Googles the sender or clicks the link. A dead or missing URL costs credibility. A clear, honest one-page site ("here is the problem, here is what we are building, we are looking for N design partners") helps modestly. It does not do the selling. Outreach does.
- Pre-product, nobody finds these sites organically. There is no SEO history and no content. Expect close to zero inbound traffic. Treat any traffic as outreach-driven and measure it that way.
- So it is not premature to have a page. It is premature to expect it to produce leads without outbound. Publishing 11 pages with no outbound motion behind each one produces 11 unread pages.

**Minimum that makes a live site useful (all required before launch):**
1. One real, monitored contact path. A real mailbox on a domain you control, or a calendar-booking link (Cal.com or similar) for a 20-minute problem-validation call. No placeholder addresses. A mailto link is acceptable and avoids any fake form.
2. An honest primary CTA, for example "Talk to us about being a design partner." Not "Sign up", "Start free trial" or "Get early access", because those imply a product exists. Interest capture should be explicit: "Join the design-partner waitlist" or "Tell us about your workflow" is fine if the copy states there is no product yet.
3. Capture without a fake signup. Options in order of preference: a mailto/booking link; a Formspree/Google Form-style "describe your problem" form with plain-language disclosure of what happens to the data; a short problem-validation questionnaire. All three are honest because they ask for a conversation, not an account.
4. Clear status line above the fold: "Pre-product. Building with design partners." No fabricated metrics, logos or testimonials, which you already avoid.
5. Legal and privacy: the DRAFT legal pages must not read as live commitments. If any form collects personal data, a short privacy notice with a real controller and contact is needed before launch (GDPR applies if EU prospects). Placeholder legal is acceptable only on pages that collect nothing.
6. Basic measurement: privacy-friendly analytics (Plausible, Umami or similar) or simply UTM-tagged outreach links, so you can say "of N people I messaged, M visited, K replied". Without this you cannot tell whether the site helps. Instrument before testing, not after.
7. Link preview that works (title, description, OG image) so the URL looks right when pasted into email or LinkedIn.

**Pilot vs all 11:**
- Pilot 1-2 sites, chosen by where outreach will actually start in the next 2 to 4 weeks, not by which site looks best. A site with no outreach behind it has no pilot value.
- Rationale: each site needs its own working inbox or booking link, its own measurement, and its own legal and privacy review. At 11 sites that is 11 monitored contact paths and 11 sets of replies you must answer fast. Unanswered inbound from a "live" site is worse than no site.
- Also an operational point: 11 near-identical sites from one owner, all public, all pre-product, can look like template spam to a prospect who finds more than one. That is a reputational risk to the whole portfolio. A pilot lets you see whether the pattern reads as credible or as spray.
- Pilot success criteria, defined up front: visit-to-reply rate from outreach, number of design-partner conversations booked, any feedback that the site confused or put people off. Suggested threshold to roll out the next batch: at least a few real conversations traced to the pilots, or clear qualitative signal that the site helped credibility. If it produces nothing in 3 to 4 weeks, the problem is the outreach, and 9 more sites would not fix it.
- Roll out in waves of 2 to 3 as outreach capacity opens, not all at once.

**Risks if ignored:**
- Activation and conversion: a site with no real contact path, or one that replies in days, gives prospects a reason to drop out right when they show interest.
- Trust and honesty: any CTA wording that implies a live product ("Sign up", "Start free trial", "Join waitlist" with no disclosure) is a dark pattern for a pre-product tool. It would damage the design-partner relationship, which depends on candor, and it is the exact thing to avoid. Check: could you explain every line of the page publicly? If not, cut it.
- Missed learning: launching 11 at once spreads attention thin and removes the ability to learn which messaging or positioning works.

**Notes on the separate public repo mechanic (outside my lens, flagged for others):**
- Public site-only repos are a sensible way to expose Pages without opening the private repos. Confirm each repo contains nothing but built site files, with no internal notes, draft strategy, contact details of real prospects, or git history that includes earlier private content. Fresh repo with a clean history is the safe default.
- GitHub Pages on a *.github.io path looks weaker than a real domain in outreach. A custom domain per business (or at least a consistent brand domain) is worth doing for the pilots because the URL is part of the credibility check.

**Dependencies on other domains:**
- Guardian/legal: sign-off that the DRAFT legal and any form data collection are acceptable for public exposure, and a privacy notice if forms collect personal data.
- Operator: one monitored inbox or booking link per pilot site, plus a response-time commitment (same business day).
- Strategist: which 1-2 businesses have outreach lists and a founder-led motion ready now, so the pilot choice is driven by real outbound.
- Advocate/messaging: wording review of the CTA and status line so nothing implies a shipped product.

**Recommendation in one line:** Launch 1-2 pilot sites with a real contact path, an honest "design partner" CTA, no fake signup, analytics or UTM tracking, and a clean public repo. Judge them on conversations booked after 3 to 4 weeks of actual outreach, then roll out the other 9 in small waves.
